themes_detail.label: Street noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 114 THIS WEEK, up 291% from the 8-week average of 29.1 per week (z-score: 3.77), suggesting a new or intensifying source of disruption in the district.
evidence: 114 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs 29.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 3.77 indicates statistically significant anomaly
291% increase suggests acute, newly emerging problem rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Identify the source: construction site, venue, commercial activity, or transportation disruption driving the spike
Interview residents in affected blocks about when noise began and impact on sleep/quality of life
Check DOB permits filed in last 90 days (375 total filings) for correlation with noise complaints by location

themes_detail.label: Damaged trees in district
themes_detail.summary: Tree damage complaints reached 10 THIS WEEK, a 1043% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week (z-score: 9.84, highest severity), suggesting recent storm damage, disease, or widespread infrastructure conflict.
evidence: 10 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 9.84 is the highest statistical anomaly in entire dataset
Spike is new and acute, not a sustained trend
reporting_angles: Determine if spike correlates with recent severe weather (wind, ice, rain) in NYC
Map complaint locations to identify if damage is clustered in specific parks or corridors (Parks data available)
Interview Parks Dept on repair timelines and whether budget (repeated CB request for park building reconstruction) is constraining response

themes_detail.label: Garbage collection failures
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints jumped to 13 LAST WEEK, up 1056% from the 8-week average of 1.1 per week (z-score: 7.35), indicating a significant sanitation service breakdown.
evidence: 13 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 7.35 indicates highly significant deviation
1056% increase suggests systemic service failure, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine cause: vehicle breakdown, staffing shortage, route realignment, or contractor failure
Identify affected blocks and interview residents on how long garbage accumulated and health/pest impact
Cross-reference with 'dirty condition' complaints (736 over 90 days) to see if uncollected waste is driving broader sanitation complaints

themes_detail.label: Boiler system failures
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints surged to 16 LAST WEEK, up 212% from the 8-week average of 5.1 per week (z-score: 4.59), during late fall when heating demands are rising and conditions are already worsening.
evidence: 16 boiler complaints LAST WEEK vs 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 4.59 is significant and timing coincides with heating season onset
Context: HEAT/HOT WATER is dominant complaint type across 90 days (8,234 total), suggesting chronic underlying infrastructure crisis
reporting_angles: Identify landlords with multiple boiler complaints and check HPD violation history and compliance patterns
Interview residents currently without heat about landlord response time and tenant rights
Investigate whether boiler spike is tied to aging building stock (375 alteration permits filed in 90 days suggest older buildings being modified rather than replaced)

themes_detail.label: Lead hazard complaints resurface
themes_detail.summary: Lead violation complaints hit 4 two weeks ago, up 220% from the 8-week average of 1.2 per week (z-score: 4.16), raising public health concerns in a historically older housing stock.
evidence: 4 lead complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Paint/plaster complaints (1,051 over 90 days) may be related: deteriorating paint is common lead source
reporting_angles: Determine which buildings generated the 4 lead complaints and cross-check with DOH enforcement history
Interview affected families about testing, remediation costs, and landlord cooperation
Investigate whether lead spike correlates with renovation activity (350 alteration permits in 90 days could disturb lead paint if not done safely)
